problemBoundary: read-only OpenSpec 1.10.0 machine observation over the existing managed-tool entrypoint; no workflow ownership or Skill/self-hosting integration
durableFacts: OpenSpec remains the only formal Change artifact authority.
The existing managed-tool resolver is the required OpenSpec runtime selection seam and does not itself invoke tools.
Policy must remain free of OpenSpec filesystem/CLI reads.
OpenSpec 1.10.0 list/status JSON provides the current formal active-Change and artifact-readiness facts required by downstream integration.
OpenSpec formal command failure can be represented as valid JSON on a non-zero exit and must not be collapsed into transport failure.
Successful observations must bind OpenSpec root.path to the exact requested repository root.
.agents OpenSpec Skills remain bootstrap development tools and are not a product runtime dependency.
proposalDirection: Add a small read-only OpenSpec integration module outside Policy.
Invoke only the validated managed OpenSpec entrypoint using the current host Node and exact repository cwd.
Expose only active Change observation and exact Change artifact-status observation justified by current consumers.
Validate the machine fields Flowkit consumes and fail closed on malformed JSON/root mismatch.
Keep observations transient; do not persist or mirror OpenSpec lifecycle state in .flowkit.
explicitNonGoals: OpenSpec mutation commands or automatic explore/propose/apply/archive
limitations: Product wrappers for OpenSpec instructions/validate/show remain deferred until a concrete Flowkit runtime consumer proves they are needed.
Mutating OpenSpec operations remain driven by existing bootstrap OpenSpec Skills during current development.
Standalone OpenSpec store support is outside the current repo-local Foundation input domain.
Whole-manager Windows/Linux acceptance remains a later Delivery Change.
